clue.text: Buckle is not commonly something potential combatants wear

parts.note: to buckle is to bend out of shape, or warp
ain't is the colloquial form of 'is not'

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a belt buckle isn't usually part of a fighter's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' marks the non-standard contraction ain't.
explanation.definitionFit: Warriors traditionally daub their faces with coloured markings before battle, so it is something fighters put on.

clue.text: Fancy that chap going after women

indicators.note: going after says the word for the chap is placed behind the letter for women

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
the pronoun for that man

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a man pursuing women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy that' reads as one exclamation, but the definition is Fancy alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A whim is a sudden passing desire or notion, much like a fancy as a noun.

clue.text: Sound shocked by Republican stench

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
eek is the cry of someone startled

explanation.surface: Someone reacting with horror to a Republican's foul smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns mean a strong, unpleasant smell, so they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Story lacking intro can still yield results

indicators.note: lacking its intro means the opening letter is missing

parts.note: a parable is a story with a moral

explanation.surface: A tale missing its opening can still deliver a satisfying outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yield results' sounds like a story's payoff; here it means land producing crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable land is fit for ploughing and growing crops, so it can still produce a harvest.

clue.text: Spy a vital tiny modification needed for seasonal pageants

indicators.note: a modification alters the order of the preceding words to produce something new

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy instructed that a small but crucial change is required.
explanation.definitionFit: School Christmas shows re-enacting the birth of Jesus are staged every December, a seasonal festive spectacle.

clue.text: A model lives in these conditions

parts.note: taken as written
to model for an artist is to sit
to live is to be, so lives gives is

explanation.surface: A fashion model living under some particular circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the present state of things, without change, matching these circumstances.

clue.text: Small change that can do widespread damage

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for a pocketful of loose coins

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: fragments flung out by an exploding shell

explanation.surface: A small adjustment that ends up causing havoc.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain shrapnel is slang for loose coins; 'Small change' looks like a minor alteration.
explanation.definitionFit: Shell fragments scatter over a wide area when a bomb bursts, and the slang sense covers jangling coins.

clue.text: Sports cars with no room for third wheel?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: small open roadsters with a driver's seat and one passenger seat

definitions.text: with no room for third wheel
definitions.note: a description: things seating only a couple
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a third wheel is an unwanted extra person with a couple, and these have space for just a pair

explanation.walkthrough: A 'third wheel' sounds mechanical, but it is the extra person tagging along with a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Many roadsters seat only driver and one passenger, leaving no space for a gooseberry companion.

clue.text: Frantically resists pet becoming something acquired following divorce?

definitions.note: acquired when a divorced parent remarries

indicators.note: frantic action is wild and disordered, so the following letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pet struggles wildly against its new owner after a family break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the new sibling arrives through a parent's remarriage after the divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: When a divorced parent remarries, that new spouse's daughter joins the family, a female sibling gained by marriage.

clue.text: A client is terribly inflexible

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written, part of the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A complaint about a very stubborn customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' does double duty: it is part of the letters as well as the verb of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without stretch or give cannot bend or adapt, so it is rigid and unyielding.

clue.text: One renting London accommodation — it follows a period in USA

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: a landlord who lets property in the capital city

definitions.text: it follows a period in USA
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Americans call the full stop a period, and a sentence after it opens in upper case

explanation.surface: A London landlord, plus a remark about something that happens in America after some stretch of time.
explanation.walkthrough: A letter is one who lets; 'period' looks like a time span but is the American name for a full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Each new sentence begins with an upper-case character after the full stop, and a London landlord is a city lessor.

clue.text: Extremely rough on East river

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outermost letters are kept

parts.note: its first and last letters
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A river described as very choppy on its eastern stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rhone flows from Switzerland through France to the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhone is a major European waterway, so it is an example of the general category.

clue.text: They require a hand when performing

definitions.text: They require a hand when performing

parts.note: surface reading: performers needing help or applause
setter's reading: these figures only move with a human hand inside them

explanation.walkthrough: 'A hand' looks like assistance or a round of applause; it is literally the hand that operates them.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric figures worn over the fist come alive only when someone's fingers work them during a show.

clue.text: Consort with mariner supplying Spooner with alcohol

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of a pair of words

parts.note: to consort with people is to mingle; it takes the S sound from the next word
an old salt is a seasoned sailor; it takes the M sound from the word before

explanation.surface: Someone socialising with a sailor who keeps the Reverend Spooner supplied with drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of MINGLE SALT. A salt is a veteran sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Single malt is whisky made at one distillery from malted barley, so it is a kind of spirit.

clue.text: Dismiss a material military order

parts.note: to fire someone is to dismiss them from a job
taken as written
twill is a woven fabric with diagonal ribs

explanation.surface: Throwing out a significant instruction from the army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like an adjective meaning relevant, but it is a fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: The command lets soldiers shoot whenever they choose, an instruction given by officers in battle.

clue.text: Central tribes hide in the same place

indicators.note: central points to the core of each word, so just the middle letters are kept

parts.note: its two middle letters
its two middle letters

explanation.surface: Tribes in the heartland conceal themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Ibid is short for Latin ibidem, used in footnotes to cite the source just mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation in references tells readers the citation comes from the identical source as before.

clue.text: Regulations blocked by alien figures

indicators.note: something blocked by an obstacle has that obstacle sitting in its path, inside it

parts.note: statutes are laws or rules
ET is the film's extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: Rules being obstructed by foreign characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figures' looks like numbers or people; it means small sculptures.
explanation.definitionFit: Small sculptures of people or animals are carved or cast figures, the usual crossword synonym.

clue.text: Sweater I unravelled in a way

indicators.note: a knitted garment that unravels comes apart and its yarn loses its order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone confessing that their jumper came apart somehow.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a hedge meaning so to speak, admitting something is true only to some degree.

clue.text: Slippery politician's career path?

parts.note: surface reading: the route taken by a devious, untrustworthy MP
setter's reading: the slick climb to the top that is hard to grip, a phrase Disraeli made famous

explanation.walkthrough: 'Slippery' looks like it describes a shifty politician, but it describes the climb itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Disraeli said he had climbed to the top of it on becoming Prime Minister, so it means a hard ascent to power.

clue.text: Celtic language employed in Somerset

indicators.note: employed in says the letters are working inside the following word

parts.note: the letters run inside the county name

explanation.surface: A Celtic tongue being used in Somerset, an English county in the south-west.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic spoken in Scotland and Ireland, one of the Celtic family.

clue.text: Funding source doesn't regularly make this, the upper limit

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adverbial answer

parts.note: a cash machine dispenses funds

indicators.note: regularly means at steady intervals, so every second letter is taken

parts.note: its second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A cash machine that does not often give the maximum.
explanation.walkthrough: ATM is the cash machine; the apostrophe in doesn't is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means no more than, giving the ceiling on an amount, the maximum allowed.

clue.text: House representatives get at Senate's corruption

indicators.note: corruption spoils the original state, so the letters before it are turned out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Members of Congress try to get at the Senate's corrupt practices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House representatives' looks like members of the US House; it means people who sell homes.
explanation.definitionFit: These agents act for vendors in selling homes, so they represent people's houses on the market.

clue.text: Reptile found when bottom of jar removed

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the final letter, the one taken off
removed tells the solver to take something away from the word

parts.note: a crock is an earthenware jar

explanation.surface: A reptile discovered once the base of a pot is taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: Croc is the informal short form for crocodile.
explanation.definitionFit: A croc is a crocodile, a large scaly creature, so it is an instance of the class.

clue.text: Starts to find every little lesion to be malign

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters, which are kept

parts.note: the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: A doctor beginning to discover that every tiny lesion is cancerous.
explanation.walkthrough: Fell as an adjective is a literary word for cruel or deadly, as in 'one fell swoop'.
explanation.definitionFit: The old adjective means fierce, cruel or deadly, sharing the sense of evil and harmful intent.

clue.text: Something bloggers hope to get, being all the same

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: a click of approval on a post
second meaning: identical, similar to one another

explanation.surface: Bloggers all chase the same thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning splits the answer into A plus a social-media approval.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things that are similar or identical, each resembling the others.

clue.text: Decide where to go for whatever food's available

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to fix a route or direction, as a ship does

definitions.note: a description of a fixed menu dish
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a fixed dish on a restaurant's menu with no choice

explanation.surface: Choosing a destination according to whatever there is to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors plot a heading before departure, and a fixed menu offers a single dish without alternatives.

clue.text: Butcher with tin fork becomes farmer

indicators.note: one letter in for another means it replaces the other in the same place

parts.note: to butcher is to slaughter, so a butcher here is one who slays
read as 't in': the letter t goes in
read as 'for k': the letter k is the one it ousts

explanation.surface: A butcher armed with a tin fork turns into a farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tin fork' must be split as 't in for k': T replaces K.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiller is one who tills the soil, ploughing and cultivating land as a farmer does.

clue.text: It's good form to make first pass

parts.note: proto- is the prefix meaning first
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Saying it is polite to make the first move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' looks like a verb; a col is a dip between peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is the accepted code of correct conduct, as in diplomatic etiquette, which is what good form means.
